title: Horribly Designed
body:
I bought the laptop for $1099.99 and I would NOT recommend. I would recommend the Lenovo Yoga 7 with the intel core ultra 5 as it has a better build, speaker location, and better fans (from what I tested in store).
Keyboard: 
The keyboard is formatted so there is no space between keys, and over time as your laptop gets more and more heated from playing games/ heavy applications such as Autocad, your keyboard warps and there is a slight wave pattern in the (middle sinks). Many useful keys are replaced for useless ones like the right FN for copilot button and f11 for HP system utility launch.
Screen:
While the screen is nice and colourful at the beginning, you can't decrease your screen brightness very much, so everyone can see what you are doing on your laptop screen (although this applies to all OLED screens so DON'T GET THEM).
Laptop Build:
The laptop is annoying to open as there is no specific place to open it from and you have to get used to opening it weirdly. Additionally, the speakers are awful and come out of the bottom. 
2 in 1 Design:
While the tablet mode is nice, if you want to look at a digital textbook and take notes at the same time  you can't since your note-taking device is your laptop. Also there are not many good note-taking apps on laptop and taking notes on Onenote (the best notetaking app I have found for windows) often is difficult to use since as you write your wrist will move the scroll bars at the bottom.
HEATING ISSUE: *****
The laptop has fans but they suck, and so it heats up INCREDIBLY quickly, leading to issues in the longevity of the laptop, as well as the keyboard warping as mentioned before. The heating issues get so bad that I have burned myself several times when touching it, also it drops all frames to 0 and I have to close the application. I have to use a fan and put it on top of my keyboard (I use an external keyboard when playing games) in order to prevent my laptop from heating up and lagging.

title: Omnibook X Flip AI PC - meets my needs very well
body: Despite challenges ordering, the Omnibook X Flip AI PC has been excellent.  Setup was easy.  I purchased it for 3 things: 1) Documents, 2) Light gaming, 3) E-reader, 4) AI.  Documents and light gaming are smooth (note: Win11 got rid of Wordpad so you need MS Office or an alternative).  My MMO runs at 1920X1200 and can go higher.  Without a strong GPU, heavy gaming is not possible.  Flip feature is cool and works smoothly.  The e-reader is a journey in itself.  From what I can tell, no Windows laptop vendor comes with a built in solution.  I tried many apps and decided on two: Aquile Reader and Sumatra PDF.  Aquile allows lots of text size/dimension tweaking and Sumatra is a lightweight PDF reader (Adobe works fine too but bulkier).  The point I'm trying to come to is the Omnibook X 16" as an e-reader is perfect with the right app.  A giant/long page is harder to read and an over-cropped page feels like a rip off.  The app puts you in control.  The X keyboard was a little "Off" at first (soft click feel and big keys) - I adapted after a week of heavy use.  For gaming, I still use external keyboard/mouse out of habit.  I have not directly used the AI capabilities but there are apps you can load (Windows comes with co-pilot).  I'm looking at GAIA.  Note: In heavy use the laptop can get warm (not hot) so I recommend a cooling pad/flow.  If taken care of the Omnibook X should provide years of service.  Enjoy.

title: Works, but not without issues
body: I purchased this laptop as a replacement for my 6 year old desktop for photo editing. Performance and screen wise, it is stunning. Shockingly fast for something this thin, and quite nice build quality. The downsides are that the fan is perpetually loud when using Adobe products, and it gets quote hot. I've had quite a few software issues as well - the touch screen randomly stopped working and the performance slowed down substantially in the first few weeks, but somehow a BIOS update fixed this. This isn't really something you'd expect to run into in the first few weeks of owning the product. The speakers are also not great, and the battery doesn't last long doing sustained work - maybe 4-5 hours max just using Adobe Lightroom. Overall, it's not great value to be honest - it does not feel like a premium experience especially given the software issues that would be very hard to troubleshoot for the average user.

title: Less “Omni,” More “Meh”
body:
I honestly can’t decide whether my disappointment is due to unrealistic expectations or whether this laptop is simply underwhelming—but I’m leaning toward the latter.

Faster startup was one of the promised improvements over my previous HP device. Unfortunately, my actual user experience determined that was a lie. The first time I tried to start the laptop after completing the initial setup and updates, it became a black mirror attached to a keyboard-shaped fidget toy, with only a tiny light in the corner to indicate that it had not completely abandoned this earthly plane. I had to force a restart—on its very first regular startup.

I hoped that was a fluke, but in less than two months, I’ve had to force-restart it at least three more times.

The speakers also have an odd effect when you aren’t positioned directly in front of or behind the device. It feels like an attempt at surround sound that only works if you sit perfectly still in precisely the right spot. The display looks good, and the sound itself is fine when everything aligns correctly.

My biggest issue, however, is performance. This laptop simply doesn’t feel like a meaningful improvement over my older device, despite speed being one of its major selling points. I may still be adjusting to the keyboard and some of the functional differences, but overall, it feels like a step backward from my previous HP Envy.

Even relatively small omissions—such as the lack of a backlit keyboard—are disappointing at this price point. Battery life appears to be good, but I find myself reluctant to use the laptop for anything beyond work because the overall experience just feels…off.

It’s difficult to capture in a single technical complaint, but I would not recommend that users who are familiar with and enjoy the HP Envy line switch to this device. It looks nice and performs adequately when it cooperates, but “adequate, when it cooperates” is not what I thought I was purchasing.

title: Great utility laptop for everyday tasks, but...
body: The HP OmniBook X Flip 16 is a decent laptop for everyday computing. It features a touchscreen and a pen input for increased interactivity, making this a good choice for people who are not that technologically proficient. However, this laptop can only go so far because it lacks a dedicated GPU, an Micro SD card reader slot, an Ethernet port, control via voice input, and internal storage expansion slots. Onboard memory and a heavy chassis weight also limit its overall appeal, especially when using the laptop in convertible tablet mode (it's extremely heavy and bulky). In conclusion, the OmniBook X Flip is a great choice for general computing but for performance computing look elsewhere.
